title: EU AI Act: Article 50 Transparency in Practice

modules.title: Identify actors and design interaction disclosure
Mark synthetic outputs and verify detection
Disclose biometric exposure and published content

concepts.name: Recognise an AI system
concepts.assessment: Distinguish an inference-based system from a simple fixed rule in a supplied case.

concepts.name: Distinguish a model from a system
concepts.assessment: Identify whether a supplier provides a model or an operated system.

concepts.name: Check the EU connection
concepts.assessment: Apply EU placement, establishment or output-use connections without treating private use or open source as universal exemptions.

concepts.name: Provider
concepts.assessment: Identify development and market/service placement under a name or trademark, including own-use service.

concepts.name: Deployer
concepts.assessment: Identify use under an actor’s authority and the personal non-professional exclusion.

concepts.name: Law, guidance and voluntary methods
concepts.assessment: Rank an operative provision, interpretative guidance and a voluntary Code in a conflict.

concepts.name: Allocate the transparency duties
concepts.assessment: Assign paragraphs 1-2 to providers and 3-4 to deployers in a two-company workflow.

concepts.name: Duties can apply together
concepts.assessment: Identify concurrent duties and explain why disclosure does not cure a prohibited use or replace other law.

concepts.name: Direct AI interaction
concepts.assessment: Distinguish conversational exchange from passive processing and genuinely human-mediated communication.

concepts.name: Assess obviousness
concepts.assessment: Evaluate the informed, observant and circumspect person standard in context rather than assuming every chatbot is obvious.

concepts.name: Check the interaction law-enforcement exception
concepts.assessment: Require legal authorisation and safeguards and restore disclosure for a public offence-reporting service.

concepts.name: Identify an agent’s principal
concepts.assessment: Choose disclosure of AI nature and the person represented, identifying the latter as Commission guidance.

concepts.name: Disclose at supervisory steps
concepts.assessment: Plan disclosures at authorisation, reporting, validation and new interactions, including uncertain downstream human contact.

concepts.name: Clear disclosure at first interaction or exposure
concepts.assessment: Reject hidden, delayed or ambiguous notifications in a supplied interface.

concepts.name: Accessible disclosure
concepts.assessment: Identify applicable accessibility requirements and select perceivable disclosure across visual and audio contexts.
concepts.source_locator: Article 50(5); Guidelines paragraph 144; Code Section 2 Measure 1.1

concepts.name: Interaction disclosure case exercise
concepts.assessment: Resolve an agent hotline scenario using actor, obviousness, exception, supervisor and accessibility checks.

concepts.name: Synthetic content
concepts.assessment: Classify generated or manipulated audio, images, video and text without equating all outputs with deepfakes.

concepts.name: Machine-readable marking versus visible disclosure
concepts.assessment: Explain why a human-visible AI badge does not itself supply machine-readable marking and detection.

concepts.name: Marking and its detection mechanism
concepts.assessment: Pair a marker with a usable verification route; do not treat a generic forensic guess as proof of provider marking.

concepts.name: Assess editing and alteration exceptions
concepts.assessment: Distinguish standard assistance and no substantial alteration of input or semantics from substantive generated changes.

concepts.name: Check the marking law-enforcement exception
concepts.assessment: Require legal authorisation to detect, prevent, investigate or prosecute rather than accepting a claimed purpose alone.

concepts.name: Assess technical quality
concepts.assessment: Evaluate effectiveness, interoperability, robustness and reliability with feasibility, costs and state of the art.

concepts.name: Compare marking methods
concepts.assessment: Compare signed metadata and watermarking through preservation and detection tests; separate Code commitments from optional methods.

concepts.name: Assess modality-specific feasibility
concepts.assessment: Distinguish free-form versus containerised text and short-text feasibility without inventing a statutory 200-token exemption.

concepts.name: Verify downstream marking responsibility
concepts.assessment: Check whether an upstream route survives the product pipeline and meets the downstream provider’s own duty.

concepts.name: Apply the targeted transition
concepts.assessment: Apply 2 December 2026 only to paragraph 2 for systems placed on the market or in service before 2 August; keep other duties on their own dates.

concepts.name: Status and scope of the Transparency Code
concepts.assessment: Explain voluntary adherence, mandatory versus encouraged measures within the Code, adequacy assessment and non-conclusive compliance evidence.
concepts.source_locator: Article 50(7); Code Sections 1-2; Commission Opinion conclusion 52

concepts.name: Keep proportionate compliance evidence
concepts.assessment: Select implementation records, detection tests and incident corrections rather than relying on a signature or marketing statement alone.
concepts.source_locator: Guidelines paragraphs 146-149; Code Section 1 Commitment 4, Section 2 Commitment 2

concepts.name: Provenance workflow case exercise
concepts.assessment: Trace generated output through edits, exports and publication; identify failed marks, detectors and responsibility handoffs.

concepts.name: Emotion recognition system
concepts.assessment: Identify inference of emotion or intention from biometric data, distinguishing fatigue and ordinary text sentiment.

concepts.name: Biometric categorisation system
concepts.assessment: Identify category assignment based on biometric data and the ancillary-service carve-out in the definition.

concepts.name: Disclose biometric exposure lawfully
concepts.assessment: Inform exposed people, check applicable data law and the narrow authorised law-enforcement allowance without treating disclosure as permission.

concepts.name: Deepfake
concepts.assessment: Apply the image/audio/video definition rather than assuming every realistic synthetic output or text is a deepfake.

concepts.name: Assess false authenticity in context
concepts.assessment: Distinguish resemblance, possible subjects and a false appearance of authenticity using the dissemination context.

concepts.name: Disclose creative and similar works
concepts.assessment: Choose appropriate disclosure that preserves enjoyment; do not treat art, satire or fiction as a total exemption.
concepts.source_locator: Article 50(4), first subparagraph; Guidelines paragraphs 120-126; Code Section 2 Commitment 3

concepts.name: Check the deepfake law-enforcement exception
concepts.assessment: Require authorised detection, prevention, investigation or prosecution; distinguish this from the different paragraph 3 wording.

concepts.name: Matter of public interest
concepts.assessment: Assess a societal-information context rather than assuming all recipes or all company communication qualify.

concepts.name: Assess the public-interest text duty
concepts.assessment: Combine AI generation or manipulation, publication and the informing purpose; distinguish internal correspondence and the authorised law-enforcement exception.

concepts.name: Human review or editorial control
concepts.assessment: Distinguish a real review/control process from an AI self-check or merely clicking publish.

concepts.name: Editorial responsibility
concepts.assessment: Identify the natural or legal person accountable for publication without substituting AI review for human accountability.
concepts.source_locator: Article 50(4), second subparagraph; Code Section 2 Commitment 4

concepts.name: Assess and evidence the editorial exception
concepts.assessment: Apply (human review OR editorial control) AND editorial responsibility; reconsider after substantive AI rewrites and avoid inventing a mandatory per-publication log.

concepts.name: Publication decision case exercise
concepts.assessment: Resolve a campaign with an avatar, synthetic interview and public-interest report; allocate duties, check lawful use and evidence proportionate disclosures.
